capture_provenance_round2: Round-2 coverage capture on the arm64 capture workstation (2026-07-25) closing pi's EXECUTE (cell 8) gap. Same PUBLISHED image, unmodified (miniobserve/pi-capture:0.80.3 = capture/pi:0.80.3), same socat/models.json ollama route, --thinking off, and — unlike the droid and opencode round-2 captures — the SAME model as this rung's s1 capture, ollama/qwen2.5:7b. It succeeded on the FIRST attempt: one bash call (rg -n TODO .) then one write. So there is NO model deviation and NO prompt-permission deviation on pi, and the 'qwen2.5:7b cannot drive a shell-tool scenario' finding from the droid and opencode lanes does NOT generalise — it is harness-specific, not a property of the model. pi also has no external-directory permission gate, so the arm's /tmp/claude/todos.txt target needed no grant (contrast opencode, which auto-rejects it headless). ONE deviation from the frameworks/pi/README invocation, and it is environmental only: HOME and PI_SESSION_DIR on a SEPARATE /pihome mount rather than the documented HOME=/workspace + PI_SESSION_DIR=/workspace/.pi-sessions, because under the documented form pi writes its own session store INTO the tree the s2 search walks, so an rg sweep would ingest the trace being captured. Scenario arm = 2026-03-15 first-run S2, live because no pi native session jsonl for S2 exists in the 2026-03 corpus. The prompt carries the same TWO added EXECUTE-steering clauses as the droid and opencode s2 freezes ('by running a shell command (grep -rn or rg -n) in the terminal' and 'and show the command you ran and its output'; 'Write' becomes 'Then write') and is BYTE-IDENTICAL to both, diff-verified, so all three harnesses share one arm. Seed is byte-identical to the droid and opencode s2 seeds (the archived S2 arm workspace minus that arm's .gitignore); the current shell-pipeline/containers/shared/workspace seed was NOT used because its main.py has TODO renamed to IMPROVE, which would make the S2 prompt match nothing. Diagnostics note: this input emits 9 'Unhandled pi record' DSL warnings and reports 4 read-but-never-present message.usage.* paths; both are PRE-EXISTING adapter characteristics, not capture defects — the frozen s1-config.jsonl emits 14 such warnings, and cell 26 fires here (4431 input / 309 output tokens), so the usage data is present via the DSL's alternate path. Since 2026-10-21 the DSL has no catch-all rule, so neither input emits 'Unhandled pi record' warnings; the catch-all had also masked unmapped paths, which the re-frozen unmapped_path_count now counts.
